intro.text: **Built for live conversations.** Pick who you're talking to, then go to **🗡️ Offense** (you bring the case) or **🛡️ Defense** (they raised an objection).

**How to use the links:** every ▶ link jumps to a live conversation where the move is demonstrated. Lines tagged **➕** are supplemental material. Double-check those before leaning on them.
Doctrinal frame: our church's Articles of Faith. One Being, three Persons; Christ has two natures; Scripture alone.

Pray first. Only the Spirit opens eyes (John 6:44; 2 Cor 4:4–6). Watch your own heart for pride; the goal is their soul, not the point (2 Tim 2:24–26). What helps in real conversations isn't knowing more verses. It's **how you run the conversation**. Use these moves every time.

moves.title: Phase 1 = agree on the plain text. Nothing else moves until they do.
moves.text: Read the verse and ask a yes/no question about what it *says* (not what it means). Don't go on until they answer. *"I'm not moving to Phase 2 until you answer Phase 1."*

moves.title: Yes/no questions, one at a time.
moves.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"* Short questions are hard to wriggle out of. Long statements give them room to filibuster.

moves.title: Call out the dodge out loud.
moves.text: When they redefine a word ("personification," "communicates information," "a vibe"), name it: *"I didn't ask about personification. I asked, can He speak?"*

moves.title: Use their rule on another verse.
moves.text: When they invent a rule for one verse (e.g. "no article = 'a god'"), apply the same rule somewhere it obviously fails (John 1:6 becomes "a man sent from *a god* named *a John*").

moves.title: Hold them to their own analogy.
moves.text: If they bring an analogy (king and messenger, software coder, three judges), don't swap it out. Push it until it proves your point: *"Can the agent of the king claim to BE the king?"*

moves.title: No topic-hopping.
moves.text: When a point lands, people often jump to "Is Jesus God?" or "the Trinity makes no sense." Don't follow. *"Let's finish this one first, then I'm happy to go there."*

moves.title: Name the goalpost shift.
moves.text: *"First you wanted a Bible verse. I gave you the verse. Now it has to come from Jesus' own mouth?"*

moves.title: "What's the only thing we do? Read."
moves.text: When they say "context," make *them* show the verse in the context. Then wait. Silence works for you.

moves.title: Ask the question back.
moves.text: End with a question they have to answer on their own (*"Who is the Father hearing from?"*), not a speech.

moves.title: Stay warm.
moves.text: Even when they rage-quit: *"I want you to be saved, brother. I love you."* Truth with love keeps the door open (1 Pet 3:15–16).

universalTools.title: "Yahweh" isn't one-person-only.
universalTools.text: Yahweh is the name of the one true God, and Scripture applies it to the Father, the Son and the Spirit. Their "then Jesus is his own Father" syllogism only works if Yahweh = the Father alone. A name can have more than one referent: "Judah" can mean a man *or* a tribe (Judges 1:1–2).

universalTools.title: Word–concept fallacy.
universalTools.text: "'Trinity' isn't in the Bible" → neither are "monotheism" or "Bible." The question is whether the *concept* is there.

universalTools.title: Three in one way, one in another.
universalTools.text: Not a contradiction. Different categories: 3 *persons*, 1 *being*. (For Muslims, hold up the Hafs, Warsh and Qalun Qurans.)

universalTools.title: Context decides literal vs. figurative.
universalTools.text: Both sides agree personification exists. But personified things don't say "set apart for **me**" or "the work **I** have called them to."

universalTools.title: "Firstborn" = rank, not birth order.
universalTools.text: David was the *youngest* son and the *second* king, yet God calls him "firstborn, the highest of the kings of the earth" (Ps 89:27).

holySpiritPlay.title: 🔥 THE HOLY SPIRIT PLAY: "the Spirit is Yahweh" (Unitarians, JWs, Oneness, Muslims)

intro.text: **Why this is the kill shot:** Unitarians spend all their energy on Jesus (agency, *shaliach*, "a god"). They usually have **no prepared answer for the Spirit**. *"Holy Spirit: kryptonite for these guys."* Two steps: **(A) the Spirit is a Person → (B) that Person is Yahweh.**

stepA.title: Step A: The Spirit is a *Who*, not a *what*

opener.text: *"Does the Holy Spirit speak? Yes or no?"*

rows.point: "Set apart for **me** Barnabas and Saul for the work to which **I** have called them." First-person speech, a choice, authority.
rows.question: *"Do actions have authority, or do persons?"* / *"He said 'I' and 'me' about Himself. That's self-awareness, right?"*

rows.point: "It seemed good to the Holy Spirit **and to us**." He takes part in a decision alongside the apostles.
rows.question: *"Can a force agree with a council?"*

rows.point: He can be grieved and rebelled against.
rows.question: *"An active force can't be offended. Whoever the Spirit is, He's someone you **can** offend."*

*"Christ is called God's power and He's a person. So being God's power doesn't rule out being a person, right?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"That's personification."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"I didn't ask about figurative language. Can He speak, yes or no? If I say 'my car told me it's not starting today,' did my car speak?"*. Then: personified wisdom never chooses missionaries in real time (Acts 13:2).

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He just communicates information / He has no mouth."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Does the Father have a mouth? Does the Father speak?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"The Father told the Spirit to say it."*
ifTheySay.youSay: The text says "for **me**… **I** have called." That's not quoting someone else.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"He's rational energy, like AI."*
ifTheySay.youSay: AI is programmed. The Spirit wills, commands and is provoked. *"Can energy be rational without personhood?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"God used the Spirit's power to create."*
ifTheySay.youSay: God also created *through Christ* (John 1:3), and Christ is a person.

ifTheySay.youSay: v.8 opens "**to** the Son He says." The Father is speaking *to* the Son. And v.10 ("You, Lord…") has no throne issue at all.

defense.objection: "John 1:1 says 'a god.' No article = indefinite."
defense.response: A predicate noun before the verb without the article describes **nature** (Harner: qualitative). "The Word was God" in nature: all that God is, the Word was.
defense.goTo: John 1:1; **1 John 4:8** (*ho theos agapē estin*); **John 1:6** (*para theou*, no article)
defense.askBack: *"Is God 'a love'? Was John sent from 'a god'? Your NWT says 'God' in 1:6. Why not in 1:1?"*

defense.objection: "*Ton theon* = the Almighty; *theos* = a lesser god."
defense.response: That's just Greek case. *Ton theon* is accusative after *pros*; *theos* is nominative. Case endings aren't ranks.
defense.askBack: *"Is the Father a lesser god when he's in the nominative?"*

defense.objection: "Firstborn of creation" (Col 1:15) = first created
defense.response: *Prōtotokos* = preeminent heir. v.16 gives the reason: "**because** by Him all things were created."
defense.askBack: *"Who was Israel's first king? Saul. So how is David 'firstborn' of the kings?"*

defense.objection: "Only-begotten" (John 3:16) = uniquely created
defense.response: *Monogenēs* = the unique, only begotten Son, never "created" (Heb 11:17: Isaac wasn't Abraham's only son).
defense.askBack: *"Was Isaac Abraham's only child?"*

defense.objection: "Beginning of the creation of God" (Rev 3:14)
defense.response: *Archē* = origin / ruler / source. He's where creation comes from.
defense.askBack: *"If you're the originator of your business, aren't you its origin?"*

defense.objection: "John 5:19: Jesus can do nothing on his own"
defense.response: That shows the Persons are distinct and act together. Finish the verse: "whatever the Father does, **the Son does likewise**."
defense.askBack: *"Does the Father do anything without the Son?"*

defense.objection: "John 14:28: 'the Father is greater than I'"
defense.response: Greater in role, in the Son's humbled human state. Not in nature. Phil 2:6–7.
defense.askBack: *"Is a husband 'greater' in nature than his wife because he leads?"*

defense.objection: "Psalm 8 / Heb 2: everything is subject to *man*, not Jesus"
defense.response: Heb 2:9 identifies the "him": "**namely Jesus**."
defense.askBack: *"Who are we going to trust, you or the author of Hebrews?"*

defense.objection: "Daniel 7: Jesus wasn't seated / Rev 3:21: believers sit on the throne too"
defense.response: Sharing kingdom authority ≠ sitting **on high** in heaven, the place that belongs to Yahweh alone (Ps 113:5).
defense.askBack: *"Show me anyone other than Jesus who sits 'on high' at the right hand of the Majesty."*

defense.objection: "Holy Spirit = active force"
defense.response: → [🔥 Holy Spirit Play](#holy-spirit-play)
defense.askBack: *"Can a force be grieved?"*

defense.objection: "Trinity isn't in the Bible."
defense.response: Word–concept fallacy. "Jehovah's Witness" isn't in the Bible as a denomination name either. Is the *concept* taught?
defense.askBack: *"Is the word 'theocracy' in the Bible?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus is Michael the Archangel."
defense.response: Scripture never says it. Michael did not dare rebuke Satan himself (Jude 9); Jesus commands him directly (Matt 4:10). God never called any angel "My Son," and **all** the angels worship the Son.
defense.askBack: *"To which of the angels did God ever say, 'You are My Son'?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was raised as a spirit, not in a body."
defense.response: He said a spirit does not have flesh and bones as He has, He showed His wounds, and He said He would raise **His body**.
defense.askBack: *"In John 2:19–21, what did Jesus say He would raise?"*

defense.objection: "Only 144,000 go to heaven."
defense.response: Right after the 144,000, John sees a great multitude **no one could count** standing before the throne, serving God in His temple.
defense.askBack: *"Where is the great multitude standing in Rev 7:9?"*

defense.objection: "The dead are unconscious. The soul stops existing."
defense.response: Paul expected to depart and **be with Christ**, away from the body and at home with the Lord. The souls under the altar speak.
defense.askBack: *"How do the souls in Rev 6:10 cry out if they don't exist?"*

defense.objection: "Hell isn't eternal. The wicked are simply destroyed."
defense.response: Jesus uses the same word, "eternal," for the punishment and for the life in one sentence.
defense.askBack: *"If the punishment isn't eternal, is the life?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus died on a stake, not a cross."
defense.response: Don't make this the fight. Thomas speaks of **nails**, plural, in His hands, and the sign was placed above His **head**. Then go back to who Jesus is.
defense.askBack: *"Why 'nails,' plural, for His hands?"*

defense.objection: "You must use God's name, Jehovah."
defense.response: The apostles take the Old Testament "name" texts and apply them to **Jesus**. Joel's "call on the name of Yahweh" becomes confessing Jesus as Lord.
defense.askBack: *"In Rom 10:13, whose name is in view, given verse 9?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus is a god, a mighty one, but not the true God."
defense.response: Jehovah says no god was formed before or after Him and He knows of no other. So is Jesus a true God or a false god? Thomas calls Him "my Lord and **my God**" and Jesus accepts it.
defense.askBack: *"Is Jesus a true god or a false god?"*

defense.objection: "People only did obeisance to Jesus, not worship."
defense.response: All the angels worship the Son. Every creature gives the same honor to God and to the Lamb. An angel refuses it; Jesus receives it.
defense.askBack: *"Why does the angel refuse what Jesus accepts?"*

defense.objection: "You need Jehovah's organization to be saved."
defense.response: Salvation is by grace through faith, not works, and not membership. When others left, Peter did not ask **where** to go, but **to whom**.
defense.askBack: *"To whom did Peter say we should go?"*

offense.title: The Angel of Yahweh claims to be God, with no "thus says the Lord"

chain.text: **Gen 31:11–13**: "the **Angel of God** said… '**I am the God of Bethel**, where you anointed a pillar and made a vow **to me**.'"
**Gen 28:12–13**: at Bethel the one who spoke was **Yahweh**.
**Gen 35:1**: God says, "go to Bethel… make an altar there **to the God who appeared to you**." *"Why is God saying 'go meet the God you met'?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Agency: a messenger speaks in the first person for the king."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"Show me the 'thus says the Lord.'"* There isn't one. *"Without it, how do you know when a messenger is speaking for God or for himself?"* Moses talking in his tent and Jonah running away weren't oracles just because they had the "messenger" title.

ifTheySay.theySay: *"Can't an ambassador speak as the king?"*
ifTheySay.youSay: **Use their analogy:** *"Can the agent of the King claim to BE the King?"* *"Yahweh can send agents, but agents can't claim to be Yahweh, or they drop dead."*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"*Malak* means a lesser being, sent by a superior."*

defense.response: "Gospel" means the good news about Jesus. And the Quran tells the people of the Gospel to judge by what they **had** in the 7th century, which was these four.
defense.askBack: *"What Gospel did Christians have in Muhammad's day?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus was sent only to the lost sheep of Israel."
defense.response: His earthly ministry went to Israel first, as promised. Then He sent His disciples to **all nations**, as Isaiah foretold.
defense.askBack: *"Who does Jesus send them to in Matt 28:19?"*

defense.objection: "The Bible has contradictions and too many versions."
defense.response: Translations are not different Bibles. The manuscript differences are known and printed in the footnotes, and no teaching depends on them. Ask for one and read it together.
defense.askBack: *"Which contradiction? Let's read it."*

defense.objection: "God can simply forgive. He doesn't need a sacrifice."
defense.response: A judge who lets the guilty go is unjust. God will by no means leave the guilty unpunished. At the cross He is both **just and the justifier**. Even the Quran ransoms Abraham's son with a great sacrifice.
defense.askBack: *"If a judge lets the guilty go free, is he a just judge?"*

defense.objection: "No one can carry another person's sins (Q 6:164)."
defense.response: The Torah the Quran confirms is built on substitution: the sins of the people laid on another. Isaiah foretold One who would bear the iniquity of us all.
defense.askBack: *"What does Isaiah 53:6 say Yahweh laid on Him?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus and His disciples were Muslims."
defense.response: His disciples worshiped Him, called Him Lord and God, and preached that He was crucified and raised.
defense.askBack: *"Would a Muslim say 'My Lord and my God' to Jesus?"*

defense.objection: "Muhammad is named in Song of Songs 5:16."
defense.response: The Hebrew word there is an ordinary word for "desirable," used by a bride about her beloved. The same word family describes Ezekiel's wife (Ezek 24:16) and Israel's children (Hos 9:16).
defense.askBack: *"Is Muhammad also in Ezekiel 24:16, where the same word is used?"*

defense.objection: "Islam is the fastest-growing religion, so it must be true."
defense.response: Truth isn't a headcount. Jesus said the many take the wide road.
defense.askBack: *"Is something true because many people believe it?"*

defense.objection: "The Quran is a miracle. No one can produce a chapter like it."
defense.response: That test has no judge and no standard. The Quran gives a better test: check with those who read the Scripture before.
defense.askBack: *"Who judges the contest, and by what standard?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus said, 'Why do you call Me good? Only God is good.'"
defense.response: He didn't say He isn't good. He asked the man **why** he said it. Jesus calls Himself the Good Shepherd.
defense.askBack: *"Is Jesus good?"*

beliefs.text: Atheist: usually "I don't believe in God" (some say "there is no God"). Agnostic: "I don't know" or "we can't know." Most hold that the universe and life came from natural causes alone and the Bible is a human book. Many see right and wrong as human-made.

lead.label: Note
lead.text: ▶ links show the move in a real conversation. ➕ marks standard classical apologetics material added so the section is complete. Same style throughout: short questions, burden on them.

lead.label: Mindset
lead.text: Scripture says every person knows God and suppresses that knowledge (Rom 1:18–21). The problem isn't missing evidence; it's the heart. The first move is to **make them define their position**, and they usually back off from "God doesn't exist" to "I don't know." Then aim at the conscience.

cheatCard.text: *"Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"* (Sets the burden.)
*"Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"*
*"Life only comes from life. Where did the first life come from?"*
*"No one dies for what they **know** is a lie."* (1 Cor 15:3–8)
*"If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know before you die?"*
**Rom 1:18–21**: they know God and suppress it. Appeal to the conscience, not just the intellect.

chain.text: *"When you say you're an atheist, are you saying God doesn't exist, or that you lack belief?"* → If it's a claim: *"How do you know?"* If it's lack of belief: *"So you don't know. Would you want to know if God has spoken?"*

ifTheySay.theySay: *"I just believe in one less god than you."*
ifTheySay.youSay: *"You already reject gods who aren't there. I'm asking about the One you already know is there."* (Rom 1:19–21)

opener.text: *"Are you claiming God doesn't exist, or that you don't know?"*

chain.text: *"Have you ever experienced something as ordered and designed as this coming from something that isn't intelligent?"*
*"Life always comes from life. That's a scientific principle (biogenesis)."* Evolution talks about life that already exists **changing**. It doesn't explain where life **came from**.
**Ps 19:1; Rom 1:20; Acts 17:24–28** ("in Him we live and move and have our being").

opener.text: *"Have you ever seen something this ordered come from something non-intelligent?"*

altOpeners.text: *"Where do you get this idea of bad from?"* (When they call something evil or unfair.)
*"What would count as evidence for you?"* (When they say there's no evidence for God.)
*"Is morality objective, or is it opinion?"* (When they say you're wrong about a moral issue.)

chain.label: Logic
chain.text: *"Are the laws of logic physical? Do they change? Where do universal, unchanging laws come from in a universe that's just matter in motion?"*

chain.label: Morality
chain.text: *"Is it **objectively** wrong to torture a child for fun? Wrong according to whom?"* → if they say it's subjective, then it's just preference. If they say it's objective, they need a transcendent standard. **Rom 2:14–15**, the law is written on the heart.

chain.label: Reason
chain.text: *"If your brain is just chemistry shaped for survival, not truth, why trust it to reason that God doesn't exist?"*

chain.label: Goal
chain.text: show they **use** God's world (logic, morality, reason) while denying Him (Rom 1:18–21; Prov 1:7). For the full approach, open [Worldviews: how do you know?](/topic/worldviews-how-do-you-know).

opener.text: *"Can I ask you about three things we both rely on every day: logic, right and wrong, and your own reasoning?"*

altOpeners.text: *"What about the people who didn't believe in Jesus, persecuted His followers, then said, 'I saw Jesus'?"* (When they say it's a game of telephone.)

chain.text: *"If Christ didn't rise from the dead, Christianity is false. Period."* (1 Cor 15:14–19) Christianity puts itself on a testable, historical claim, and God has given proof to all by raising Him from the dead (Acts 17:31).

chain.label: Facts
chain.text: crucified publicly under Pilate · the tomb was guarded · the disciples fled as cowards, then died boldly · hostile skeptics were converted (Paul the persecutor, James the doubting brother). *"Why would eyewitnesses and enemies suffer and die for what they **knew** was a lie?"*

opener.text: *"If Jesus really rose from the dead, would you become a Christian?"*

closer.text: *"If heaven and hell were real, wouldn't you want to know now? You wouldn't want to wait until you die to find out."*

defense.objection: "Jesus is a copy of Horus / Osiris / Mithras."
defense.response: Comes from pop media (*Zeitgeist*, *Religulous*), not the Egyptian sources. No virgin birth, no crucifixion, no resurrection in the primary texts.
defense.askBack: *"Which primary Egyptian text says Horus was born of a virgin? Name it."*

defense.objection: "It's like the Salem witch trials / a game of telephone."
defense.response: Public execution under Pilate, guarded tomb, and **eyewitnesses** who were still alive when it was written (1 Cor 15:6, "most are still alive").
defense.askBack: *"Who dies for what they know is a lie?"*

defense.objection: "Why do babies get cancer because Adam ate fruit?"
defense.response: Federal headship. A head affects those he represents, like a mother's toxins affecting her unborn child. Adam's fall broke creation. Christ, the second Adam, restores it.
defense.askBack: *"If God exists, wouldn't you expect Him to fix the fall? He did, in Christ."*

defense.objection: "If God knew I'd reject Him, why create me? That's unjust."
defense.response: God is just and owes no one mercy. No one is forced to reject Him: people reject Him because they love their sin, and they are responsible for it. Hell is the just penalty for real guilt, not a mistake. Yet God *freely* offers Christ to all who come, and no one who comes is turned away.
defense.goTo: Rom 9:19–21; John 3:19; Ezek 33:11; John 6:37; Rom 1:24 ("God **gave them up**")
defense.askBack: *"Is there anything you've done that a perfectly just judge should ignore?"*

defense.objection: "A jealous God who demands worship is vain."
defense.response: Not all jealousy is sinful. A husband who's jealous over an unfaithful wife is **rightly** jealous. God made every breath you take, so He has a rightful claim.
defense.askBack: *"If your wife slept with another man, would your jealousy be ugly, or just?"*

defense.objection: "Heaven/hell is a game show: pick a door."
defense.response: It's not a game show. It's a **command and an invitation**. God commands everyone to repent and offers Himself, the greatest good. Whoever refuses Him is responsible for that refusal.
defense.askBack: *"It's not God playing games. You're playing games with Him."*

defense.objection: "So many religions. How would I know which one?"
defense.response: God has spoken, and He proved it publicly by raising Jesus from the dead. Only Christianity rests on a public resurrection, an event that is **historically testable**.
defense.askBack: *"Which other religion stakes everything on a public event you can investigate?"*

defense.objection: "Who created God?"
defense.response: The question assumes everything needs a cause. It doesn't. Only what **begins to exist** needs a cause. God never began; He is uncaused by definition, the cause of everything outside Himself. Asking who made Him is a category mistake, like asking who made the One who was never made.
defense.askBack: *"Does everything need a cause, or only things that begin to exist?"*

defense.objection: "I'm not 100% sure. I have doubts."
defense.response: Faith isn't intellectual perfection. Jesus welcomes doubters who come to Him.
defense.askBack: *"Do you believe Christ died for your sins and rose again? Will you turn from your sin and trust Him as Lord?"*

defense.objection: "There's no evidence for God."
defense.response: Creation itself is the evidence: a universe that began, runs on laws, and holds minds and morals. And God gave proof to all by raising Jesus from the dead.
defense.askBack: *"What would count as evidence for you?"* Then: *"Is the problem the evidence, or that you don't want God to be there?"*

defense.objection: "Science has disproved God."
defense.response: Science studies how creation works. It depends on order and laws it cannot explain, and it cannot tell you why anything exists or what is right.
defense.askBack: *"Which experiment showed there is no God?"*

defense.objection: "If God is good, why is there so much evil and suffering?"
defense.response: Calling something evil assumes a real standard of good. Scripture names the cause (the fall), shows God turning evil to good, entering suffering at the cross, and promising to end it.
defense.askBack: *"By what standard do you call it evil?"*

defense.objection: "The Bible was written by men and is full of errors."
defense.response: Men wrote as they were moved by the Holy Spirit. Ask for a specific error and read it together.
defense.askBack: *"Which error? Let's look at it."*

defense.objection: "The God of the Old Testament is a moral monster."
defense.response: To judge Him you need an objective standard, which only He supplies. He judged wicked nations after centuries of patience, He takes no pleasure in the death of the wicked, and He bore judgment Himself at the cross.
defense.askBack: *"If there is no God, what makes anything objectively wrong?"*

defense.objection: "Religion causes wars, and Christians are hypocrites."
defense.response: People sin, which is exactly what the Bible says. Jesus condemned hypocrisy harder than anyone. Judge Christianity by Christ.
defense.askBack: *"Does a counterfeit bill prove there's no real money?"*

defense.objection: "I'm a good person. I don't need God."
defense.response: Good by whose standard? By God's law, none is righteous, and breaking one point makes us guilty of all. Then give the gospel: Christ died for sinners.
defense.askBack: *"Have you ever lied, stolen, or hated someone? What does that make you before a perfect Judge?"*

defense.objection: "Evolution explains life. We don't need a Creator."
defense.response: Change in living things doesn't explain the first life, the information inside it, or the universe it lives in. And Scripture says God made everything in six days and made man directly, in His image. We are not the product of evolution.
defense.askBack: *"Where did the first life, and the information in it, come from?"*

defense.objection: "Miracles are impossible."
defense.response: Only if there is no God, which assumes the answer. If God made the universe, raising a man is not hard for Him.
defense.askBack: *"If God created everything, is a resurrection too hard for Him?"*

defense.objection: "What about people who have never heard?"
defense.response: Everyone has creation and conscience, and everyone suppresses them. No one is condemned for not hearing, but for sin. The Judge of all the earth will do right. And you have heard.
defense.askBack: *"You've heard. What will you do with Jesus?"*

defense.objection: "Faith is believing without evidence."
defense.response: Biblical faith is trust in a Person on good grounds: eyewitness testimony and many convincing proofs.
defense.askBack: *"Do you trust anyone on the basis of testimony?"*

defense.objection: "Jesus never existed."
defense.response: Paul received the resurrection report within a few years and met Peter and James, the Lord's brother, in person.
defense.askBack: *"Who did Paul meet in Galatians 1:18–19?"*

intro.text: Winning the argument saves no one. Christ does. Say the whole message plainly, call for a response, and leave the results to God.

lines.label: God saves; you are faithful
lines.text: your job is to say the truth clearly. God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; Rom 1:16; John 6:44)

lines.label: Law before grace
lines.text: a person has to see their sin and God's judgment before the cross makes sense to them. (Rom 3:19–20; Gal 3:24)

lines.label: Jesus is Lord
lines.text: the call is to repent and follow Christ, not to repeat a prayer or add Jesus to a life that stays the same. (Luke 9:23; Rom 10:9; Acts 20:21)

lines.label: No false promises
lines.text: the gospel offers forgiveness and Christ Himself, not health, wealth or an easier life. (Phil 3:8; Mark 8:36; 2 Tim 3:12)
God created all things and made us for Himself. He is holy and just, He cannot overlook sin, and He will judge every person. (Gen 1:1; Isa 6:3; Hab 1:13; Acts 17:24–31; Heb 9:27)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What do you think happens after we die?"*

Every one of us has broken God's law. We are not basically good people who slip up; we are dead in sin, and the wages of sin is death. No amount of good works can pay it off. (Rom 3:10–12; Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Eph 2:1–3; Isa 64:6)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Have you kept God's law perfectly?"*

God the Son became man, lived the sinless life we have not lived, and died in the place of sinners, bearing the wrath they deserve. He was buried, rose bodily on the third day, and is Lord of all. (John 1:14; Isa 53:5–6; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 3:18; Rom 5:8; 1 Cor 15:3–4; Phil 2:9–11)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Why did Jesus have to die?"*

God commands all people everywhere to repent. Whoever turns from sin and trusts in Christ alone is forgiven and has eternal life: by grace, through faith, not by works. Following Him costs everything, and no one who comes to Him is turned away. (Mark 1:15; Acts 17:30; John 3:16; Eph 2:8–9; Rom 10:9–13; Luke 14:27–28; John 6:37)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What is keeping you from turning to Christ today?"*

sections.heading: The short version: the Romans Road

lines.text: When you only have a minute, walk these in order, and call them to repent. (Rom 3:23; Rom 6:23; Rom 5:8; Acts 17:30; Rom 10:9–10; Rom 10:13; Rom 8:1)

sections.heading: How to walk someone through it

lines.text: For a step-by-step way to do this in a real conversation, using the Ten Commandments first and then the cross, open [The Way of the Master](/topic/the-way-of-the-master).

Pray with them. Get them a Bible and get them into a church that preaches it, where they can be baptized by immersion as a believer. Follow up. Don't pronounce them saved. Point them to Christ, and let assurance grow from following Him. (Acts 2:41–42; Matt 28:19–20; 2 Cor 13:5; 1 John 2:3–6; John 8:31)
Stay warm and leave the door open. You plant and water; God gives the growth. (1 Cor 3:6–7; 1 Pet 3:15–16; 2 Tim 2:24–26)

topics.title: The Way of the Master

intro.text: God opposes the proud but gives grace to the humble (James 4:6), so: law to the proud, grace to the humble. The Ten Commandments work like a mirror: they show a person their sin so that the cross makes sense. Jesus did this with the rich young ruler. (Rom 3:19–20; Rom 7:7; Gal 3:24; Mark 10:17–22)

lines.text: Move from ordinary talk to spiritual things with one question.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What do you think happens after we die?"*
Almost everyone says yes. Let them say it. (Prov 20:6)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would you consider yourself a good person?"*

sections.heading: 3. Have you kept the Ten Commandments?

lines.text: Walk through a few, one at a time, and let them answer each. (Ex 20:1–17)

lines.label: Lying
lines.text: *"Have you ever told a lie? What does that make you?"*

lines.label: Stealing
lines.text: *"Have you ever taken anything that wasn't yours, whatever its value?"*

lines.label: God's name
lines.text: *"Have you ever used God's name as a curse word?"*

lines.label: Lust
lines.text: Jesus said that looking with lust is adultery in the heart. *"Have you ever done that?"* (Matt 5:27–28)

lines.label: Hatred
lines.text: Jesus put anger under the command "You shall not murder" (Matt 5:21–22), and John says whoever hates his brother is a murderer (1 John 3:15).
Sum up what they admitted in their own words, then ask. (Heb 9:27; Rom 2:15–16; James 2:10)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"If God judges you by that standard, will you be innocent or guilty?"*
Don't soften it, and don't gloat. Say it because you care where they end up. (Rev 21:8; 1 Cor 6:9–10)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would that be heaven or hell? Does that concern you?"*
You stand guilty in God's courtroom, and Someone steps in and pays your fine in full. That is what Christ did on the cross, and He rose from the dead. (Rom 5:8; 2 Cor 5:21; 1 Pet 2:24; 1 Cor 15:3–4)
Believing a parachute exists won't save you; you have to put it on. Turn from sin and put your trust in Christ alone, today. (Acts 3:19; Acts 20:21; Rom 13:14; 2 Cor 6:2)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"When are you going to do that?"*
**Already humble?** If someone is broken over their sin, skip the law and go straight to grace.

lines.label: Aim at the conscience
lines.text: answering objections clears the path, but the law and the gospel do the work. Don't spend an hour on arguments and never get here. (Rom 2:15)

lines.label: Tone
lines.text: kind, patient, and plainly concerned for them. (2 Tim 2:24–26)
Then go back to [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel) for the full message and what to do when they respond.

topics.title: Worldviews: how do you know?

intro.text: A presupposition is what a person takes for granted before the argument starts. The atheist is not neutral, and neither are you. He already knows God and suppresses that truth (Rom 1:18–21), so you are not handing him a God he has never met. You are showing him that he leans on God every time he reasons, judges or trusts his own mind. (Prov 1:7; Col 2:3; Ps 14:1; 1 Cor 1:20)

lines.text: You are not saying he knows nothing or believes in nothing. He reasons, does science and knows right from wrong, because he lives in God's world and is made in God's image. You are saying his worldview cannot **account for** any of it, and yours can. He is using the tools God gave him to argue against God.

lines.label: Say
lines.text: *"We both use reason. I'm not asking whether you reason. I'm asking why reason can be trusted if your view is true."*

sections.heading: Step 1: Don't give up your ground

lines.text: Do not agree to set the Bible aside and argue from "neutral" facts. No one is neutral, and Scripture is the standard, not the thing on trial. You start from what God has revealed. He starts from his own guess. (Prov 26:4; 2 Cor 10:5; 1 Pet 3:15)

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Would you set aside your trust in reason to prove reason? Then why should I set aside God's word?"*

sections.heading: Step 2: Ask what he would accept

lines.text: Before you give evidence, find out what he counts as evidence. If he has no standard, he has no basis for saying there isn't any.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"What would count as evidence for you?"*
**"Only what can be measured or tested."** → *"Did you measure that? Which experiment showed that only tested things are true?"* That rule is not something the five senses can find.
**"I don't know what would convince me."** → *"Then how do you know there's no evidence?"*
**"God is outside the universe, so He can't be tested."** → Evidence is more than lab results. We reason, weigh testimony and draw conclusions every day. (Acts 1:3; Heb 11:1)

sections.heading: Step 3: Step into his view and show it cannot stand

lines.text: Take his view on its own terms and ask what follows. One question at a time, and wait for the answer. (Prov 26:5)

lines.label: Knowledge
lines.text: *"How do you know that? How do you know anything for certain?"* If he says we can't know anything for certain: *"Are you certain of that?"*

lines.label: Logic
lines.text: *"Are the laws of logic made of matter? Do they change? Where do unchanging, universal laws come from in a universe of matter in motion?"* If he says God is illogical: *"That assumes logic is reliable. In your view, where does it come from?"*

lines.label: His own mind
lines.text: *"You said 'mind.' Is that anything more than brain chemistry? If your thoughts are chemistry shaped for survival, why trust them to tell you what is true?"*

lines.label: Science
lines.text: *"Why expect nature to act tomorrow the way it did today?"* (Gen 8:22; Col 1:17; Heb 1:3)

lines.label: Meaning
lines.text: *"If we came from nothing and go to nothing, on what basis does anything you do matter?"* If he says nothing has meaning: *"Does that sentence have meaning?"* (Eccl 1:2; Eccl 12:13–14)
Start here when he calls something evil, unfair or hateful.

lines.label: Ask
lines.text: *"Is morality objective, or is it opinion?"*

**"It's subjective."** → *"Then you can't say I'm wrong. You can only say you prefer something else, the way one person prefers burgers and another pizza."* Watch for him to keep saying you are wrong anyway. Point it out kindly.
**"It comes from my experience."** → *"Someone raised to hate his neighbors has experience too. Is his hatred good?"* Experience differs from person to person, so it cannot be the standard.
**"It comes from science."** → Science tells you what **is**. It cannot tell you what **ought** to be. *"Which experiment shows that lying is wrong?"*

**"That's just your interpretation of the Bible."** → Everyone interprets something: he interprets data and his own experience. Disagreement does not cancel truth. *"If someone says 1 + 1 = 3, does that make the answer uncertain?"*
**"That's true for you. This is my truth."** → An opinion is not the same as truth. Truth is what matches reality, whoever believes it. *"Can a person sincerely believe something and be wrong?"*
**"It's objective."** → *"Then who set the standard, and why does it bind everyone?"* (Rom 2:14–15)

sections.heading: Step 4: Bring him back to your ground

lines.text: Show that what he has been borrowing belongs to God. Logic reflects God's unchanging mind, morality His holy character, the order of nature His faithfulness, and our reasoning His image in us. All things were made through the Word. (Gen 1:27; Mal 3:6; John 1:1–3; Acts 17:24–28)
**"So you're saying atheists can't know anything?"** → No. He knows a great deal. The question is whether his worldview can explain how.
**"I just lack belief. I don't have to prove anything."** → *"You still reason, judge and trust your mind every day. What do those rest on?"*

**"That's circular. You're using God to prove God."** → Every final starting point has to vouch for itself, or it isn't final. *"Can you prove your words have meaning without using words?"* The question is which starting point makes sense of everything else. His explains nothing. God's word explains logic, morality, science and him. (Heb 6:13)

**"We both just assume our senses work."** → For him the senses are the foundation, with nothing under them. For you they are a tool, and under them is the God who made eyes, minds and the world they fit.
**"Logic is just a fact of the universe."** → That repeats the claim; it doesn't explain it. *"Would you accept it if I said God is just a fact of the universe?"*
**"Logic is just how humans think."** → Then it could have been otherwise, and it would not bind anyone who thinks differently, including you.
**"Morality comes from evolution or society."** → That tells you what people **do** approve of, not what they **ought** to. Was slavery right when society approved it?
**"I don't know where they come from, and that's fine."** → *"So you rely on them with no reason to. That is faith. I can tell you where they come from."*
**Don't say "you believe in nothing."** He will name things he believes, and he'll be right. Say his worldview can't account for them.
**Don't call him or his view dumb, and don't dismiss him.** Say "that doesn't hold together," and stay kind when he gets sharp. (2 Tim 2:24–26)

**Don't blame evil on God's hands being tied.** When evil or hell comes up, don't say God wanted to stop it but free will prevented Him. God is sovereign over all things, He is not the author of sin, and people answer for their own sin. Use [the evil and suffering answer](/atheist/objection/if-god-good-why-there) and [the "why create me?" answer](/atheist/objection/if-god-knew-id-reject). (Eph 1:11; Gen 50:20; Acts 2:23)
**Don't trade away creation to sound reasonable.** God made everything in six days. See [the evolution answer](/atheist/objection/evolution-explains-life-we-dont).
**Don't treat it as a trick.** Winning the exchange saves no one. He is not confused; he is suppressing the truth, and only God opens blind eyes. (2 Cor 4:4–6; 1 Cor 2:14)
**Evidence still belongs.** The apostles pointed to the empty tomb and the eyewitnesses. Give the evidence as God's facts, not as something a neutral judge gets to rule on. (Acts 17:31; 1 Cor 15:3–8)
**Get to the cross.** This clears the ground. Then give [The Gospel](/topic/the-gospel).
For a short version to run live, open [the borrowed capital play](/atheist/case/play-3).

intro.text: One Being, three Persons: the Father, the Son and the Holy Spirit. One *what*, three *who's*. Each line below is taught in Scripture; the Trinity is what you get when you believe all of them at once.

lines.text: (Deut 6:4; Isa 43:10; Isa 44:6; 1 Cor 8:4; James 2:19)
(John 1:1; John 8:58; John 20:28; Col 2:9; Titus 2:13; Heb 1:8)
For the full argument, open [The Holy Spirit play](/holy-spirit).

The Father sends the Son, the Son prays to the Father, and the Spirit is sent by both. All three are present at Jesus' baptism. (Matt 3:16–17; Matt 28:19; John 14:16–17; John 15:26; John 17:5; Gal 4:4–6; 2 Cor 13:14)

lines.text: that is tritheism. Scripture says there is one God.

lines.text: that is Arianism. All things were made through the Son (John 1:3).

lines.text: The New Testament survives in thousands of Greek manuscripts, some copied within a few generations of the originals. The Dead Sea Scrolls, copied before and around the time of Christ, agree closely with the Hebrew manuscripts copied a thousand years later. (Isa 40:8; Matt 24:35; 1 Pet 1:24–25)
The writers were eyewitnesses or wrote down what eyewitnesses told them, while many witnesses were still alive to object. (Luke 1:1–4; 2 Pet 1:16; 1 John 1:1–3; 1 Cor 15:3–8)

sections.heading: Jesus treated Scripture as God's word

lines.text: He quoted it as final, said it cannot be broken, and said every part of it would be fulfilled. (Matt 4:4; Matt 5:17–18; John 10:35; Luke 24:44)
Men spoke from God as they were carried along by the Holy Spirit, so the Scriptures as first written are without error. (2 Tim 3:16–17; 2 Pet 1:20–21)
The suffering Servant, the pierced hands and feet, the birthplace of the Messiah and the pierced One were all written long before Jesus was born. (Isa 53; Ps 22; Mic 5:2; Zech 12:10)

topics.title: Words they use

lines.label: Jehovah
lines.text: their preferred form of God's name (YHWH). For them it names the Father only.

lines.label: New World Translation (NWT)
lines.text: the Watchtower's own Bible translation.

lines.label: Watchtower / Governing Body
lines.text: the leadership that directs all Witness teaching and calls itself the "faithful and discreet slave."

lines.label: Active force
lines.text: their term for the Holy Spirit, whom they say is not a person.

lines.label: Kingdom Interlinear
lines.text: the Watchtower's own Greek and English New Testament. Useful because it prints the Greek with a word-for-word English line next to their NWT.

lines.label: The 144,000
lines.text: the "anointed" who they say go to heaven. Everyone else hopes for life on a paradise earth.

lines.label: Biblical Unitarian
lines.text: holds that God is one person, the Father, and Jesus is a human Messiah.

lines.label: Arian
lines.text: holds that the Son is God's first and greatest creature.

lines.label: Shaliach (agency)
lines.text: the Jewish idea that a sent agent stands for the one who sent him. They use it to explain away texts where Jesus speaks as God.

lines.label: Oneness / modalism
lines.text: God is one Person who shows Himself as Father, Son and Spirit (as roles or modes, not three Persons). Oneness Pentecostals say that one Person is Jesus.

lines.label: Homoousios
lines.text: "of the same essence," the Nicene term for the Son's relation to the Father.

lines.label: Malak / angelos
lines.text: Hebrew and Greek for "messenger." It names a job, not a nature.

lines.label: Godhead
lines.text: for them, three separate beings who are one in purpose.

lines.label: Exaltation
lines.text: the teaching that faithful people can become gods.

lines.label: Great Apostasy
lines.text: their claim that the true church was lost after the apostles.

lines.label: Restoration
lines.text: their claim that Joseph Smith restored the church.

lines.label: Standard works
lines.text: their four books of scripture: the Bible, the Book of Mormon, the Doctrine and Covenants (D&C), and the Pearl of Great Price.

lines.label: JST
lines.text: the Joseph Smith Translation, his revision of the Bible.

lines.label: Testimony / burning in the bosom
lines.text: an inner feeling taken as God's confirmation that the church is true.

lines.label: King Follett discourse
lines.text: Joseph Smith's 1844 sermon teaching that God was once a man.

lines.label: Tawhid
lines.text: the absolute oneness of Allah.

lines.label: Shirk
lines.text: associating anything with Allah. The one sin Allah will not forgive if a person dies in it (Q 4:48).

lines.label: Isa
lines.text: the Quran's name for Jesus.

lines.label: Tawrat, Zabur, Injil
lines.text: the Torah, the Psalms and the Gospel, which the Quran says Allah revealed.

lines.label: Tahrif
lines.text: the claim that the earlier Scriptures were corrupted.

lines.label: Hadith
lines.text: reports of what Muhammad said and did.

lines.label: Surah / ayah
lines.text: a chapter and a verse of the Quran.

lines.label: Tafsir
lines.text: commentary on the Quran.

lines.label: Hafs, Warsh, Qalun
lines.text: different transmitted readings of the Quran.

lines.label: Atheist
lines.text: does not believe in God. Some go further and say there is no God.

lines.label: Agnostic
lines.text: says they don't know, or that no one can know.

lines.label: Naturalism
lines.text: the view that nature is all there is.

lines.label: Objective morality
lines.text: right and wrong that are true whatever anyone thinks.

lines.label: Burden of proof
lines.text: whoever makes a claim has to back it up. "There is no God" is a claim.

lines.label: Trinity
lines.text: one God in three Persons. See [The Trinity](/topic/the-trinity).

lines.label: Two natures
lines.text: Jesus is one Person who is truly God and truly man.

lines.label: Monogenes
lines.text: the unique, only begotten Son. It marks His unique, eternal relationship to the Father, never creation (LSB: "only begotten").

lines.label: Prototokos
lines.text: Greek for "firstborn." In texts like Col 1:15 (cf. Ps 89:27) it means the preeminent heir, not the first one created.

lines.label: Arche
lines.text: Greek for "beginning," "origin" or "ruler."
